question: Your CI pipeline runs Claude Code with the -p flag to review every pull request. The reviews flag patterns that your team accepts, and they miss your team's own criteria, such as the rule that each new API endpoint needs an integration test. The team wants every CI run in the repository to apply these criteria automatically. What is the most effective way to give Claude Code these criteria?

options.text: Add the review criteria to the user-level CLAUDE.md file in the home directory of the developer who maintains the pipeline, so Claude Code applies them to reviews.
options.reason: User-level CLAUDE.md is personal and is not shared through the repository, so the CI runs do not receive this project context.

options.text: Configure the pipeline to pause each review and ask the pull request author to type the team's review criteria before Claude Code starts.
options.reason: CI runs Claude Code in non-interactive mode with -p, so waiting for typed input would make the pipeline hang instead of supplying context.

options.text: Document the review criteria and testing standards in the project-level CLAUDE.md file committed to the repository, so every CI run loads them as context.
options.reason: The guide names CLAUDE.md as the mechanism for giving CI-invoked Claude Code project context such as testing standards and review criteria.

options.text: Add --output-format json with --json-schema to the pipeline command, so the structured findings follow the team's review criteria.
options.reason: These flags enforce the structure of the output for machine parsing, but they do not give Claude Code the team's review criteria.
